newsitem.title: USA: US EPA gets big response in air standard comments.
newsitem.headline: US EPA gets big response in air standard comments.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said Wednesday it received thousands of comments on its plan to raise air quality standards.
As the public comment period closed, EPA said it received more than 17,000 letters, 3,000 e-mail messages and 15,000 phone calls to a special "800" number.
That is in addition to comments from four public hearings held across the country on the agency's controversial proposal to tighten standards against soot and smog pollution.

"As EPA begins the task of analyzing these comments, we are mindful of our responsibility, under the law, to give them utmost consideration in the setting of the new public health standards," EPA Administrator Carol Browner said in a statement.
U.S. Public Interest Research Group said it delivered more than 4,000 comments to EPA on the last public comment day in support of stronger standards.
The National Association of Manufacturers also filed comments on the last day, opposing stronger standards.
NAM said it represents more than 10,000 small business members, and "has a special concern for the impact the proposed (revised standards) will have on small business."
